intellectual_tasks.name: Intellectual tasks
intellectual_tasks.description: Activities that acquire, interpret, document, or analyze task-relevant information and formulate decisions or plans

sub_categories.name: Information Processing
sub_categories.description: Acquire, interpret, measure, or document task-relevant information
primitives: Listen to or observe instructions or signals

sub_categories.name: Problem Solving
sub_categories.description: Analyze conditions and requirements to identify application locations or issues, estimate resources, select tools and materials, or formulate designs and plans
primitives: Inspect to check state or find issues
Estimate time, materials, labor and cost
Select and procure tools and materials
Prepare design, layout or installation plans

primitives.name: Take measurements
primitives.description: Perceive readings from a level, scale, gauge, or digital measurement. The reading can be abstract, such as level balance, or numeric, textual, or digital.
examples: Measure a level balance to determine whether it is perfectly horizontal or vertical
Read a pressure gauge

primitives.name: Determine tool-application location
primitives.description: Determine the point, line, or area where a tool should be applied
examples: Identify the point to drill or make a hole
Determine the location of the cap of a nail gun

primitives.name: Inspect to check state or find issues
primitives.description: Inspect something to determine the location and cause of a problem or issue
examples: Inspect a roof for problems

primitives.name: Study plan, instruction or specifications
primitives.description: Read plan, instruction or specifications to determine work activities
examples: Read specification on an air compressor

primitives.name: Listen to or observe instructions or signals
primitives.description: Listen to instructions or see communication signals from others

primitives.name: Prepare records, documents, and reports
primitives.description: Maintain records, files, and document actions, and progress reports
examples: Write a report on a project

primitives.name: Estimate time, materials, labor and cost
primitives.description: Estimate the amount of time, materials, labor and cost needed to complete a task
examples: Estimate materials and labor required to complete roofing jobs

primitives.name: Select and procure tools and materials
primitives.description: Select suitable tools or materials and arrange for them to be ordered or purchased
examples: Select and order lumber
Select and purchase tools or surface finishes for painting jobs

primitives.name: Prepare design, layout or installation plans
primitives.description: Prepare a design or sketch, or plan the layout, installation, or repair of construction systems according to plans, specifications, and codes
examples: Plan the layout and installation of electrical wiring
Prepare a sketch showing equipment locations

social_tasks.name: Social tasks
social_tasks.description: Activities that exchange information and coordinate work with other people

sub_categories.name: Coordinating
sub_categories.description: Convey information through speech or gestures and schedule or coordinate work with others
primitives: Use gestures to signal other workers
Schedule and coordinate work with others

primitives.name: Talk to convey information
primitives.description: The use of spoken words to convey information
examples: Speak to a fellow worker about a project

primitives.name: Use gestures to signal other workers
primitives.description: Use hand, arm, or body movements to signal other workers
examples: Hand signal a crane operator

primitives.name: Schedule and coordinate work with others
primitives.description: Schedule and coordinate work with other workers to complete a task
examples: Coordinate with a fellow worker to lift a heavy object

physical_tasks.name: Physical tasks
physical_tasks.description: Embodied activities that manipulate tools or objects or exert physical effort on the work environment

sub_categories.name: Finger manipulation
sub_categories.description: Manipulate controls, tools, or objects primarily through finger motion or force, with little gross arm movement
primitives: Pull or push an object with fingers

sub_categories.name: Arm translation and positioning
sub_categories.description: Translate, place, or position a tool or object through coordinated hand and arm movement
primitives: Pull or push an object with arm
Move tool along a linear path

sub_categories.name: Arm and wrist rotation
sub_categories.description: Rotate or reorient the arm, wrist, tool, or object to apply force, change orientation, or collect and transfer material
primitives: Twist an object using wrist rotation
Pivot a tool about a fixed point
Swing arm while holding an object

sub_categories.name: Mixing motion
sub_categories.description: Use repeated, circular, or wrapping motions to agitate, combine, or secure materials

sub_categories.name: Surface-contact manipulation
sub_categories.description: Move a tool while maintaining controlled contact with a work surface to mark, cut, spread, or stroke

sub_categories.name: Whole-body locomotion
sub_categories.description: Use the legs and torso to move between locations, climb, or transport an object
primitives: Carry an object to a location

sub_categories.name: Whole-body load handling
sub_categories.description: Use whole-body force and postural control to manipulate heavy objects or bend and straighten the body
primitives: Pull or push a heavy object
Pick or place a heavy object

primitives.name: Pull or push an object with fingers
primitives.description: Grasp something firmly with fingertips and pull it with finger force to detach it or push it to attach it to something. May require wrist movement, but does not require arm force
examples: Open the cap of a nail gun
Plug an air tool into an air compressor
Open the water outlet on an air compressor

primitives.name: Press an object with fingers
primitives.description: Press or squeeze an object with the inner part of the fingers
examples: Press a button to turn on an air compressor
Press release button on a utility knife to take out the blade
Squeeze a lubricant bottle to dispense lubricant
Pull trigger of an power screwdriver to fasten a screw
Pull trigger of a nail gun to shoot a nail
Spray insulation foam

primitives.name: Open fingers
primitives.description: Open fingers briefly to release an object before grasping again
examples: Open fingers briefly to let a plumb bob hang freely

primitives.name: Rotate an object with fingertips
primitives.description: Move the fingers in a circular direction to hold and tighten something along a thread or operate a valve. A large object may require all fingers and wrist motion, while a small object can be rotated with two or three fingers.
examples: Adjust a pressure valve on an air compressor (large)
Tighten a straw onto a spray can (small)

primitives.name: Grab an object
primitives.description: Take a hold of something quickly with single arm or both arms.
examples: Grab the thread of a plumb bob to stop it at the desired location

primitives.name: Pull or push an object with arm
primitives.description: Grasp something firmly with all or some fingers and pull it with arm force to detach it from something or push it with arm force to attach it to something
examples: Open a spray can
Extend a measuring tape
Attach a cord to an electrical socket
Push drill bit of a power drill into an object to make a hole
Open a door

primitives.name: Pick or place an object
primitives.description: Pick up or place a discrete object within reach of the arms using one or both hands
examples: Pick up a trowel
Place an electrical box on the floor

primitives.name: Position an object
primitives.description: Position, place, or align a tool or object for use or application at a location. Hold the object in the air without dropping it or placing it on a surface.
examples: Position a lubricant bottle
Position an electrical cord at a wall socket

primitives.name: Move tool along a linear path
primitives.description: Move tool in a linear path to apply something to a surface or move the tool towards a target location.
examples: Move a sealing gun along a joint to apply sealant
Dip a paint brush into a paint can

primitives.name: Twist an object using wrist rotation
primitives.description: Twist an object with the wrist to tighten or loosen it along a thread or to operate a valve
examples: Rotate a pressure valve on an air compressor

primitives.name: Pivot a tool about a fixed point
primitives.description: Pivot a tool about a fixed point to apply force to an object
examples: Rotate a wrench to tighten a bolt

primitives.name: Swing arm while holding an object
primitives.description: Swing the arm in a circular motion with the elbow as the pivot point
examples: Swing a hammer to hit a nail

primitives.name: Shake an object
primitives.description: Shake the arm with repeated back-and-forth motion
examples: Shake a spray can

primitives.name: Reorient an object
primitives.description: Change the orientation of an object with a wrist or arm motion. This can be done with one or both hands.
examples: Flip a shingle to the other side
Change orientation of a brick

primitives.name: Pour liquid from a container
primitives.description: Pour liquid from a container by tilting the container to allow the liquid to flow out
examples: Pour a mixture into a container

primitives.name: Scoop material with a tool
primitives.description: Collect and lift loose, granular, or viscous material by inserting a tool into or beneath the material
examples: Scoop mortar with a trowel
Scoop soil with a shovel

primitives.name: Stir liquid and solid mixture
primitives.description: Stir a mixture of liquid and solid with a tool in a circular motion
examples: Stir mortar with a trowel

primitives.name: Wrap around, tie or untie
primitives.description: Wrap a string, rope, or cord around an object and tie it in a knot
examples: Wrap a rope around a post and tie it in a knot
Untie the knots on a plumb bob

primitives.name: Mark on a surface
primitives.description: Mark with a pencil or chalk on a surface to plan an action
examples: Mark with a pencil along a speed square
Mark a point on a wall to fasten a screw

primitives.name: Cut an object
primitives.description: Cut something with a single forward or backward motion or repeated back-and-forth motion.
examples: Cut a stud with an electric saw
Cut shingles with a utility knife

primitives.name: Spread object on surface
primitives.description: Rub a tool on a surface to apply or spread something
examples: Rub a trowel on a surface to spread mortar

primitives.name: Stroke tool on surface
primitives.description: Rub a tool on a surface gently to smooth or finish it
examples: Use a brush to paint on a surface
Use a roller to paint on a surface

primitives.name: Walk to a location
primitives.description: Walk empty-handed to a location
examples: Walk to a wall to inspect it

primitives.name: Carry an object to a location
primitives.description: Carry a light tool or object with one arm or both arms to a location
examples: Carry a spray can (single arm)
Carry a felt paper (bimanual)

primitives.name: Climb up or down
primitives.description: Climb up or down stairs or a ladder
examples: Climb up a ladder

primitives.name: Pull or push a heavy object
primitives.description: Pull or push a heavy object resting on a surface to position and align it. This can require one or both hands.
examples: Adjust a wall cabinet on a rack

primitives.name: Pick or place a heavy object
primitives.description: Pick up or place a heavy object with both arms
examples: Pick up a ladder
Place a wall cabinet

primitives.name: Carry a heavy object
primitives.description: Carry a heavy object using both hands, holding the object from below or from the side
examples: Carry a wall cabinet

primitives.name: Bend down or straighten up
primitives.description: Bend down at the waist to pick up an object and straighten up to stand
examples: Pick up a leaf blower from the ground
Pick up a saw from the floor
Bend down and pick up a stud from the ground
